based_on: NIBS-DAS v1.0-beta, from the template repository at https://github.com/danieltcorp/nibs-das_repo. The column list below is taken VERBATIM from the header row of nibs-das_examples/mep_example/collated_participant_data/nibs-das_mep_exampledata_2026-02-04.xlsx, not from the manuscript text, because the example file is what the Big NIBS data platform actually receives. Preprint: doi:10.64898/2026.04.30.720417.
_notes: Columns are the STUDY-INVARIANT part of the format. The per-muscle measure columns (mep_ampl_fdi, pre_rms_fdi, ...) are generated at export time from the Channel column of _trials.csv, so they are described by 'measures' below rather than listed here.

'source' says where the value comes from in this tool. 'trials' is a column of _trials.csv; 'participants' is a column of participants.tsv; 'nibs' is a field key in nibs_bep037.json; 'setting' is an add-on setting; 'derived' is computed at export.
A field this tool cannot supply is written blank. A blank in a shared dataset is honest. A guessed value is a wrong number that nobody downstream can detect.

columns.name: age
columns.description: Age in years. Integer in the example file.

columns.name: sex
columns.description: Free text in the example file: 'Male', 'Female'. NOT the BIDS M/F codes, so values are passed through unchanged rather than normalised.

columns.name: handedness
columns.description: Free text in the example file: 'Right', 'Left'.

columns.name: ManufacturerModelName
columns.description: Stimulator model, e.g. 'BiStim2'. The name drops the possessive 's' relative to BIDS because NIBS-BIDS v6.3 renamed it; nibs_bep037.json already emits the v6.3 spelling, so this is a straight copy and not a correction.

columns.name: protocol_name
columns.description: The block or paradigm a trial belongs to, e.g. 'SICI'. NOT the same question as tms_stim_mode: in the example file every row is protocol_name SICI while tms_stim_mode alternates single and dual, because the test-alone and conditioned trials of one SICI block share a protocol and differ in mode.

columns.name: waveform
columns.description: Lowercase in the example file ('monophasic'), whereas the NIBS-BIDS vocabulary is capitalised ('Monophasic'). Lowercased on export.

columns.name: current_direction
columns.description: 'normal' in the example file, i.e. the stimulator's normal/reverse setting, which is FirstInflection in NIBS-BIDS terms rather than the cl/co winding vocabulary. Mapping is ambiguous and is left to the add-on setting when it cannot be resolved.

columns.name: targeting_method
columns.description: 'manual' in the example file. NIBS-BIDS uses 'scalp-heuristic' and 'fixed-position' for the same idea, so the vocabularies do not line up exactly.

columns.name: pulse_intensity_rmt
columns.description: Percent of resting motor threshold for the first (conditioning) pulse. 80 in the example.

columns.name: second_pulse_intensity_rmt
columns.description: Percent of resting motor threshold for the second (test) pulse. 120 in the example. Blank for single-pulse protocols.

columns.name: inter_stimulus_interval
columns.description: Interval between the paired pulses, in ms. 2 in the example, which is a SICI interval. Note the NIBS-BIDS field of the same name (InterStimulusInterval) means the interval BETWEEN trials and is in seconds; this column is the within-pair interval, so the two must not be confused.

columns.name: tms_pos_centre
columns.description: Stimulation site, e.g. 'Left_M1'. Underscore-joined in the example file.

columns.name: rmt_intensity
columns.description: Measured resting motor threshold as percent of maximum stimulator output. 56 in the example.

columns.name: trial_number
columns.description: Chronological trial number within a participant, from 1. Segment_Overall rather than Segment because Segment restarts per stimulus type, so with two stimulus types it would number two different trials the same. In the example file this runs 1 to 40 with no gaps, meaning rejected trials are not represented at all.

columns.name: tms_stim_mode
columns.description: Whether the trial delivered one pulse or two. Resolved from the trial's stimulus label through stim_mode_vocabulary below.

_notes: The muscle suffix comes from the Channel column of _trials.csv, lowercased and slugified. Channel is free text the user typed, so a study recording 'First Dorsal Interosseous' produces a valid but non-conventional suffix. The original-to-slug mapping is written into the export sidecar rather than guessed at.
Only channels actually recorded produce columns. A study with FDI and APB gets each measure twice; a single-channel study gets each once.

standard.name: mep_ampl
standard.description: Peak-to-peak amplitude of the evoked response. Already mV in _trials.csv and mV in the example file, so no conversion.

standard.name: pre_rms
standard.description: RMS of the pre-stimulus window. Same units as the signal, i.e. mV, though the _trials.csv column name does not say so.

extended.name: mep_lat
extended.description: Onset latency of the evoked response. Resolved per trial from a manual marker, the consensus across onset detectors, or the single selected detector, in that order; mep_lat_source says which applied.

extended.name: mep_lat_source
extended.description: Which method produced mep_lat on this trial: manual, consensus, detector, or none. Categorical, not a measurement, hence no units. Carried per trial rather than stated once per file because the fallback varies within a file: agreement can fail on one trial and succeed on the next. Without it a collated latency column mixes definitions with no way to separate them, which is the condition that makes a pooled analysis unsound.

extended.name: mep_dur
extended.description: Onset to offset duration of the evoked response.

extended.name: hreflex_ampl
extended.description: H-reflex amplitude, where the stimulus type is an H-reflex rather than a cortical stimulus. Shares a source column with mep_ampl; which name applies is a property of the stimulus, not of the arithmetic.

measures._extended_status: NOT AGREED. NIBS-DAS v1.0-beta defines mep_ampl and pre_rms only. The names above follow their own {measure}_{muscle} pattern rather than inventing a parallel convention, but they are this tool's proposal and nothing more until the NIBS-DAS authors adopt them. Written only when the add-on's extended-measure setting is on, which is off by default, so that a default export cannot pre-empt the vocabulary decision. mep_lat_source needs raising separately: it is the first entry here that is provenance rather than a measurement, so it takes a slot in a per-muscle measure block without being a measure, and NIBS-DAS may prefer such a field elsewhere entirely. It is placed beside mep_lat because it qualifies mep_lat and must not be separable from it by a column selection.

unmapped.problem: NIBS-DAS has no trial-status column. In the example file trial_number runs 1 to 40 with no gaps, so rejected trials are simply absent and a reader cannot distinguish a study that rejected nothing from one that dropped its rejections before export.
A trial containing ADC-saturated samples has an underestimated amplitude. Without a flag it appears in the collated file as an ordinary, and lower, number.
The amplitude unit was not declared by the source file and was assumed. The collated format states mV by convention with no way to say the value is unverified.

_notes: Matched case-insensitively against the alphabetic characters of the stimulus label only, so 'sici', 'SICI_80' and 'ICF120' all resolve. Kept here rather than in code because these labels are lab-specific and will need editing without a release; the add-on settings override this list.
A label matching neither list exports blank, and the unmatched labels are named in the run log. A guessed 'single' on a paired-pulse trial is a wrong number nobody downstream can detect.
